abstract.text: Occlusion relationship reasoning based on convolution neural networks consists of two subtasks: occlusion boundary extraction and occlusion orientation inference. Due to the essential differences between the two subtasks in the feature expression at the higher and lower stages, it is challenging to carry on them simultaneously in one network. To address this issue, we propose a novel Dual-path Decoder Network, which uniformly extracts occlusion information at higher stages and separates into two paths to recover boundary and occlusion orientation respectively in lower stages. Besides, considering the restriction of occlusion orientation presentation to occlusion orientation learning, we design a new orthogonal representation for occlusion orientation and proposed the Orthogonal Orientation Regression loss which can get rid of the unfitness between occlusion representation and learning and further prompt the occlusion orientation learning. Finally, we apply a multi-scale loss together with our proposed orientation regression loss to guide the boundary and orientation path learning respectively. Experiments demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results on PIOD and BSDS ownership datasets.

citations.context: Occlusion relationship reasoning recovers occlusion relationship between objects from monocular images, which is promotion and important for a variety of computer vision research areas, such as object detection [4, 1], scene understanding [17], segmentation [4, 23, 3] and 3D reconstruction [15].

Previously, a number of traditional methods extract occlusion boundary by image segmentation and then recover occlusion relationship on the basis of boundary by designing hand-crafted features or adding extra prior information, e.g. [8, 16, 12, 14].
DOC [19] uses two networks for occlusion boundary pixel classification and occlusion orientation regression respectively.

DOOBNet [18] designs an unified end-to-end multi-task deep object occlusion boundary detection network to simultaneously predict object boundary and occlusion orientation by sharing convolutional features.
OFNet [10] considers the importance of occlusion cues for two tasks, and designs two sub-networks to share occlusion cues.

Previous methods, such as DOOBNet [18], OFNet [10] first use the backbone network to extract different level features and use the entire decoder to extract shared information for two tasks, which improve the effect of occlusion reasoning but ignores the different effects of different level features on boundary and orientation.
Previous methods [19, 18, 10] infer the occlusion orientation by regressing a continuous orientation value.
Experiments prove that we achieve state-of-the-art results on both PIOD [19] and BSDS ownership [13] datasets.
We achieve new state-of-the-arts results on two challenging benchmarks including PIOD [19] and BSDS ownership dataset [13].
Deng et al. [2] use a bottom-up/top-down architecture to predict crisp boundaries.
Based on HED [20], CED [22] implements edge enhancement by adding a decoder structure.
CEDN [21] utilizes a fully convolutional encoder-decoder network to focus on detecting higher-level object contours.
DOOBNet [18] adopts an encoder-decoder structure with skip connection to recover occlusion boundaries and occlusion relationship.
For example, HED [20] gets multi-scale boundaries by supervising the different side-layer output results.
BDCN [5] performs different supervision on different side-layers to optimize side output results.
DOC [19] proposes using the pixel-based orientation variable to represent the occlusion orientation relationship and regression to estimate the orientation variable.
DOOBNet [18] limits the predicted occlusion orientation θ̂ to the ranges [−π, π) and regress the orientation value within the ranges.
In our network, as shown in Fig. 2, we use ResNet [6] as a base feature extraction model as in previous works [18, 11, 10].

Different from the method of supervised encoders that are widely used for edge detection [20, 22, 9, 5], we output and supervise the side-layer result of the decoder, which makes the lower-stage get the guide of occlusion information, thereby recovering more accurate boundary results.
This block can strengthen the recognition ability of each stage, benefited from the architecture of ResNet [7].

Compared with the former orientation regression method [19, 18], our OPR loss has the following advantages: 1) we address the periodicity problem of the occlusion orientation representation fundamentally and avoid the bad effect of improper and inaccurate loss computation; 2) unlike directly regression the orientation value, we utilize the network to learn the orthonormal vector pair and the relation of orthonormal vector pair to mediately recover the occlusion orientation.
We evaluate the proposed approach on two public datasets: PIOD [19] and BSDS ownership dataset [13].

For the evaluation metrics [18, 10], we use the Boundary Map Recall (BPR) and Oritation Maps Recall (OPR) with three-level measure: the Fixed Contour Threshold (ODS), the Best Threshold of Image (OIS), the Average Precision (AP).
We compare our approach with recent methods including SRF-OCC [16], DOC-HED [19], DOC-DMLFOV [19], DOOBNet [18], OFNet [10].
Finally, we visualize the boundary maps and occlusion relationship maps of our models and others including the DOOBNet[18] and OFNet[10].

sections.summary: Motivates DDNet by identifying two problems: previous single-decoder methods do not respect the differing stage needs of boundary extraction and orientation inference, and continuous orientation regression struggles with periodicity. Reviews encoder-decoder, multi-scale supervision, and prior occlusion-orientation representation methods, and lists contributions: dual-path decoding, orthogonal orientation representation with OOR loss, and state-of-the-art results on PIOD and BSDS ownership.
sections.title: Introduction and Related Work

sections.summary: Introduces the DDNet decoder: share occlusion information in higher stages via the Occlusion-Shared Module, then split into boundary and orientation paths in lower stages. Explains why boundary path benefits from layer-by-layer recovery and multi-scale supervision through Feature Fusion and Separation blocks, while orientation path uses skip connections. Describes Feature Boost Residual blocks and how decoder side outputs are fused for boundary prediction.
sections.title: Dual-path Decoder Network

sections.summary: Presents orthogonal occlusion orientation representation: decompose orientation θ into a horizontal vector a and vertical vector b, with θ=atan2(b,a), to avoid periodicity problems. Defines Orthogonal Orientation Regression (OOR) loss using smoothL1 on the normalized vector relation. Then formulates overall training loss as boundary loss plus weighted orientation loss, with class-balanced cross-entropy for boundary and OOR applied only at boundary pixels.
sections.title: Orthogonal Orientation Regression and Training

sections.summary: Covers datasets (PIOD and BSDS ownership), implementation details, metrics (BPR/OPR at ODS/OIS/AP), and comparisons with SRF-OCC, DOC, DOOBNet, and OFNet. Reports DDNet's state-of-the-art results on both datasets. Ablations examine number of shared high stages, continuous orientation vs orthogonal vectors, and amount of multi-scale supervision. Concludes with qualitative boundary/orientation visualizations and summary that the dual-path decoder, multi-scale supervision, and OOR loss improve occlusion relationship reasoning.

Previous methods, such as DOOBNet [18], OFNet [10] first use the backbone network to extract different level features and use the entire decoder to extract shared information for two tasks, which improve the effect of occlusion reasoning but ignores the different effects of different level features on boundary and orientation.
Previous methods [19, 18, 10] infer the occlusion orientation by regressing a continuous orientation value.
Experiments prove that we achieve state-of-the-art results on both PIOD [19] and BSDS ownership [13] datasets.
We achieve new state-of-the-arts results on two challenging benchmarks including PIOD [19] and BSDS ownership dataset [13].
Deng et al. [2] use a bottom-up/top-down architecture to predict crisp boundaries.
Based on HED [20], CED [22] implements edge enhancement by adding a decoder structure.
CEDN [21] utilizes a fully convolutional encoder-decoder network to focus on detecting higher-level object contours.
DOOBNet [18] adopts an encoder-decoder structure with skip connection to recover occlusion boundaries and occlusion relationship.
For example, HED [20] gets multi-scale boundaries by supervising the different side-layer output results.
BDCN [5] performs different supervision on different side-layers to optimize side output results.
DOC [19] proposes using the pixel-based orientation variable to represent the occlusion orientation relationship and regression to estimate the orientation variable.
DOOBNet [18] limits the predicted occlusion orientation θ̂ to the ranges [−π, π) and regress the orientation value within the ranges.
In our network, as shown in Fig. 2, we use ResNet [6] as a base feature extraction model as in previous works [18, 11, 10].

Different from the method of supervised encoders that are widely used for edge detection [20, 22, 9, 5], we output and supervise the side-layer result of the decoder, which makes the lower-stage get the guide of occlusion information, thereby recovering more accurate boundary results.
This block can strengthen the recognition ability of each stage, benefited from the architecture of ResNet [7].

Compared with the former orientation regression method [19, 18], our OPR loss has the following advantages: 1) we address the periodicity problem of the occlusion orientation representation fundamentally and avoid the bad effect of improper and inaccurate loss computation; 2) unlike directly regression the orientation value, we utilize the network to learn the orthonormal vector pair and the relation of orthonormal vector pair to mediately recover the occlusion orientation.
We evaluate the proposed approach on two public datasets: PIOD [19] and BSDS ownership dataset [13].

For the evaluation metrics [18, 10], we use the Boundary Map Recall (BPR) and Oritation Maps Recall (OPR) with three-level measure: the Fixed Contour Threshold (ODS), the Best Threshold of Image (OIS), the Average Precision (AP).
We compare our approach with recent methods including SRF-OCC [16], DOC-HED [19], DOC-DMLFOV [19], DOOBNet [18], OFNet [10].
Finally, we visualize the boundary maps and occlusion relationship maps of our models and others including the DOOBNet[18] and OFNet[10].

sections.summary: Motivates DDNet by identifying two problems: previous single-decoder methods do not respect the differing stage needs of boundary extraction and orientation inference, and continuous orientation regression struggles with periodicity. Reviews encoder-decoder, multi-scale supervision, and prior occlusion-orientation representation methods, and lists contributions: dual-path decoding, orthogonal orientation representation with OOR loss, and state-of-the-art results on PIOD and BSDS ownership.
sections.title: Introduction and Related Work

sections.summary: Introduces the DDNet decoder: share occlusion information in higher stages via the Occlusion-Shared Module, then split into boundary and orientation paths in lower stages. Explains why boundary path benefits from layer-by-layer recovery and multi-scale supervision through Feature Fusion and Separation blocks, while orientation path uses skip connections. Describes Feature Boost Residual blocks and how decoder side outputs are fused for boundary prediction.
sections.title: Dual-path Decoder Network

sections.summary: Presents orthogonal occlusion orientation representation: decompose orientation θ into a horizontal vector a and vertical vector b, with θ=atan2(b,a), to avoid periodicity problems. Defines Orthogonal Orientation Regression (OOR) loss using smoothL1 on the normalized vector relation. Then formulates overall training loss as boundary loss plus weighted orientation loss, with class-balanced cross-entropy for boundary and OOR applied only at boundary pixels.
sections.title: Orthogonal Orientation Regression and Training

sections.summary: Covers datasets (PIOD and BSDS ownership), implementation details, metrics (BPR/OPR at ODS/OIS/AP), and comparisons with SRF-OCC, DOC, DOOBNet, and OFNet. Reports DDNet's state-of-the-art results on both datasets. Ablations examine number of shared high stages, continuous orientation vs orthogonal vectors, and amount of multi-scale supervision. Concludes with qualitative boundary/orientation visualizations and summary that the dual-path decoder, multi-scale supervision, and OOR loss improve occlusion relationship reasoning.
